t: The Reverse Centaur's Guide to Life After AI
tz: 《反向半人馬：AI 之後生活指南》
publisher: Verso Books (UK); MCD / Farrar, Straus and Giroux (US)
en: A "centaur" is a person whom technology makes stronger. A "reverse centaur" is the opposite: a delivery driver, warehouse worker or coder forced by software to work at a machine's pace. Cory Doctorow, author of Enshittification, uses this idea to ask who AI is really for. He argues that much of the AI boom is hype fuelled by investors who need endless growth, that chatbots are useful but cannot do many of the jobs bosses hope to replace, and that the bubble could hurt the wider economy. He is not anti-AI and uses it himself. A short, punchy read for anyone who wants a clear-eyed view of AI at work.
zh: 「半人馬」係指借科技令自己更強嘅人；「反向半人馬」就啱啱相反：送貨司機、倉務員、程式員，被軟件逼住用機器嘅速度做嘢。寫過《Enshittification》嘅 Cory Doctorow 用呢個比喻問一個問題：人工智能究竟係為邊個服務？佢認為好多 AI 熱潮只係投資者為咗追求無限增長而炒作出嚟；聊天機械人有用，但做唔到老闆想取代嘅好多工作；而呢個泡沫大到可能拖累成個經濟。佢唔係反對 AI，自己都有用。篇幅短、講得爽快，啱想冷靜睇清 AI 點樣影響工作嘅讀者。

reviews.d: Persuasive and reassuring on AI hype, but the confident tone grates; too early to call, as railways and dotcom survived their bubbles.
reviews.dz: 講AI炒作有說服力，但語氣太篤定；鐵路同科網都捱過泡沫。

reviews.d: A "wonderful" book: shows LLMs are useful but not truly intelligent, and that their gains go to a narrow group of insiders.
reviews.dz: 好書：講清大型語言模型有用但唔算真正有智能，好處只落入少數人手。

ken: Ask of any AI tool: does it make the worker a centaur, or turn them into a reverse centaur?
kzh: 用任何 AI 工具前問一句：佢令工人變成半人馬，定係反向半人馬？
